thread:
Olivia: Quick heads-up — ran a head-to-head comparison between v2 quantized and fp16 variants using the replay harness. Seeing an unexpected p95 regression on long-context (2k) requests.

Olivia: Summary: same prompts, same decode params, tokenizer validated. Synthetic harnesss (synth-load) looked fine, but replay shows higher tail latency. Suspect kernel selection for matmul + KV path.

Marco: Can you paste the bench command and profiler snippet?

Olivia: Sure — command: 
```
bench_replay --model=gptx-8q-v2 --replay=/replays/longctx-2k.json --decode='{"temp":0.0,"top_p":0.9,"max_tokens":256,"stop":["\n\n"]}' --batch=auto --profile=lite
```
Profiler top lines: 
```
matmul_int8_v2           p50 12ms p95 38ms
kv_cache_lookup         p50 1.4ms p95 4.8ms
attn_forward_fused_fp16 p50 9ms p95 12ms
other_overhead          p50 3ms p95 5ms
TOTAL                   p50 28ms p95 65ms
```

Olivia: Note kernel selected = matmul_int8_v2 on the critical matmul. On synth-load we got TOTAL p95 ~42ms. Replay shows 65ms.

Jen: Did we accidentally enable continuous batching or a different batch window for replay? That could interact badly with the KV hot-path.

Olivia: Batch window: same config for both runs -- batch=auto; runtime decided batch=16 for synth and batch=8 for replay (due to arrival patterns).

Sam: Two quick hypotheses: 1) matmul_int8_v2 has worse perf with longer KV rows (sequence=2k -> larger KV buffers causing less cache-friendly tiling), 2) replay requests have prefix overlap causing KV cache misses on continuous batching.

Anya: Any chance tokenizer alignment differs? Even tiny tokenization diffs can change lengths and stop sequences, shifting memory layout.

Olivia: Tokenizer check: I re-ran on first 1000 prompts with the same tokenizer binary and seeds; token counts identical. Stop sequences validated. So not tokenization.

Rui: Could be kernel autotuner choosing int8 path because it marginally wins on median, but tail suffers for edge inputs. We should try forcing kernel selection to fp16 matmul for longctx.

Marco: Agreed. Try a quick run forcing kernel override and a pinned batch size to isolate arrival pattern.

Olivia: Will run two quick replays and post results: 1) --runtime-flag set-kernel:matmul=fp16 2) --batch=16 --runtime-flag set-kernel:matmul=int8_strict

perf-bot: Enqueued job 2101234600 for Olivia: replay-run (longctx, kernel overrides). ETA ~8m. :hourglass_flowing_sand:

Olivia: Results (short):
- fp16 forced: TOTAL p95 44ms (p50 21ms)
- int8_strict + fixed batch=16: TOTAL p95 46ms (p50 20ms)
- previous auto-int8 + replay: TOTAL p95 65ms (p50 28ms)

Olivia: So forcing fp16 or forcing int8 with fixed batch both tighten tail significantly. That points to interplay between kernel selection heuristics and variable batch sizing on replay arrival patterns.

Sam: Interesting. So autotuner + adaptive batching yields suboptimal tail for this workload. We need a deterministic fallback for longctx: prefer fp16 when seq_len>1k or when KV memory per item > threshold.

Jen: For benchmarks we should record arrival pattern (interarrival CDF) and annotate runs. Otherwise apples-to-apples claims are weak. Add fields: arrival_distribution, batch_window_ms, kernel_override.

Anya: Also add a small tokenizer-checksum (sha256 of token ids) to metadata so downstream can validate exact tokenization alignment.

Rui: I'll open a runtime PR to: 1) log the kernel selection reason code path and metric (why int8 chosen), 2) allow policy rules like prefer-fp16-for-longseq, 3) expose batch-window used per-run.

Marco: Can we add an E2E micro-benchmark that replays the same arrival trace across synth and replay harnesses to prove the hypothesis? e.g., synth -> replay the traced interarrival times.

Olivia: Good call. I'll export the arrival timeline and run it through synth-load. If that reproduces the tail, then it's arrival pattern. If not, it's the actual payload differences.

perf-bot: Olivia's job 2101234600 completed. Artifacts: /artifacts/2101234600/{profiler.json,arrival_trace.json,bench.log}

Olivia: Follow-up notes I left in bench.log: kernel selection heuristic checks quantized_gain_score and cache_tile_fit. We hit a borderline score 0.49 where int8 was chosen. Need to adjust threshold for long sequences.

Anya: Let's capture this as a short guideline in the benchmark playbook: 1) always record token checksum, arrival CDF, batch decisions, kernel reason. 2) run kernel-forced controls (fp16 and int8) as part of apples-to-apples comparison. 3) include kv-size distribution.

Sam: Also flag a possible perf regression: if autotuner changes threshold, future deploys could flip kernels and regress tails. Add canary with tail-SLO gate.

Olivia: Agree. I'll open a ticket and attach the logs. Thanks all. :thumbsup:

Rui: Thanks — PR and ticket links coming shortly.

Jen: Great convo. Quick action items in ticket: bench metadata schema, runtime logs, threshold tweak trial, and canary test.

Olivia: Done — ticket INF-3287 created with attachments.
